analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: one row is added at head line 2371 to the failure-modes table. It documents that a cold load can be refused (503 or insufficient memory) while an idle model is resident, because that slot holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. Held slots are excluded from eviction (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel) and their weights get no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes). The row links to model-autopilot.md and ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift.

This is documentation only. The patch contains no code, authorization, attestation, crypto or data-handling change. It touches no trust boundary (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011) and no asset or threat control, including T-041 cache posture, which is unchanged. The base text in the supplied units is unchanged context.

Remaining question: the described Autopilot hold behavior lives in source files not supplied here (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift, model-autopilot.md). I could not verify that code. The hold could affect availability: if hold expiry or an operator's ability to place holds is unbounded, a hold could starve cold loads. The row says the hold expires, but that was not checked against source. No threat-model entry covers Autopilot placements, so the next pass may want to confirm that hold duration is bounded and that holds are not remotely controllable by an adversarial party such as a consumer or the coordinator. This is not a finding because the evidence shows documentation only.
